tier1.text: Pseudopodia are temporary extensions of a cell that help it move and feed. In the body, white blood cells called macrophages use pseudopodia to move through tissues. Pseudopodia also let macrophages squeeze through the walls of capillaries, the smallest blood vessels. Cytoplasm, a cell's inner material, flows into a pseudopod, and the whole cell follows.

quotes.quote: A temporary protrusion or retractile process of a cell, associated with flowing movements of the protoplasm, and serving for locomotion and feeding.

quotes.quote: A macrophage is an irregularly shaped phagocyte that is amoeboid in nature and is the most versatile of the phagocytes in the body. Macrophages move through tissues and squeeze through capillary walls using pseudopodia.
